title: The short-job trade-off
hook: Clearing tiny tasks first can delay the long task’s own deadline.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that short-jobs-first can push a long job past its deadline, so with deadlines the long job may need to go first even though total waiting rises

misconception: Short jobs first is always the best order.
objective: Compare waiting and lateness when their objectives conflict.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Clearing tiny tasks first can delay the long task’s own deadline. For this long job due at minute 25, which order meets its deadline? Correct option: Long job first. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.

recall.question: Three 5-minute jobs and a 20-minute job due at minute 22 are all ready. If you do the short jobs first, when does the long job finish?
recall.why: 5 + 5 + 5 + 20 = 35, past minute 22; starting the long job first would finish it at 20.
